## Motivation and setup

Black-hole entropy is a count of microscopic states, but identifying exactly which states are counted can be subtle. In strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ Yang–Mills theory, known supersymmetric black holes occupy a four-dimensional sheet inside a five-dimensional space of conserved charges. It might seem that exponentially many supersymmetric states exist only near this sheet. This paper proposes a broader picture: a black hole can share charge with supersymmetric excitations outside its horizon, producing large entropy away from the single-black-hole locus.

The five charges are three electric or R-charges $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$ and two angular momenta $J_1,J_2$. Their gravitational setting is type IIB theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The analysis concerns the leading large-$N$ entropy, with charges of order $N^2$. It uses known black-hole thermodynamics and motivated conjectures to predict where different kinds of supersymmetric states dominate.

The paper distinguishes an ordinary degeneracy from the superconformal index. A degeneracy counts states at definite charges. The index instead makes a signed count that combines states along lines in charge space. The direction of these lines is

$$
t_{I}=\frac{1}{2}\left(1,1,1,-1,-1\right).
$$

Moving along this direction increases the three electric charges while reducing the two angular momenta, without changing the charge combinations resolved by the index. Consequently, an index coefficient cannot automatically be interpreted as the number of states at one particular point. Even where an index line intersects the black hole sheet, other points along it may contain more states.

This observation motivates the two separate questions addressed in the paper: what is the entropy at specified values of all five charges, and which contribution survives as the leading term after taking the signed sum along an index line? The proposed answers rely on different conjectures and carry different levels of evidence.
:::

::: {.summary-section}
## Construction and results

The first ingredient is a black hole dressed by supersymmetric excitations. Grey galaxies place angular momentum in a distant gas of high-spin gravitons. Dual dressed black holes place electric charge in dual giant gravitons. Revolving black holes, related to supersymmetric descendants, can share the leading thermodynamics of grey galaxies. The gas or dressing carries a substantial fraction of the charge, while the black-hole core supplies the leading entropy.

The charges split as

$$
Z_{i}=Z_{i}^{BH}+Z_{i}^{gas},
$$

Here $Z_i$ denotes the five charges collectively. The core charges lie on the black hole sheet, while the macroscopic gas charges are nonnegative. At leading order, the proposed components can be treated as noninteracting for the purpose of adding charges and evaluating entropy. The dressed concentration conjecture then prescribes the maximization

$$
\max_{Z_{i}^{\prime}}S_{BH}(Z_{i}^{\prime}),~~~(Z_{i}^{\prime}\leq Z_{i}~~~\forall i=1\ldots 5)
$$

The optimization ranges over allowed black-hole cores. Rather than restricting large entropy to a thin sheet, it extends that entropy into the surrounding charge space. An algorithm identifies the optimal core and which charge components reside in the dressing. The resulting microcanonical ground-state diagram has eleven phases: the pure black-hole phase, three grey-galaxy phases, and seven dual-dressed phases.

![Figure 1. A $\mathbb B^3$ slice of the black hole sheet. Blue equal-charge planes separate the cores of the three rank-two dual-dressed phases; their surfaces seed the rank-four phases and their intersection seeds the rank-six phase. The red equal-angular-momentum plane separates the two rank-two grey-galaxy cores and seeds the rank-four grey-galaxy phase. ([arXiv:2501.17217](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17217))](../assets/papers/2501.17217/b3slices.png){fig-alt="A ball divided by blue equal-electric-charge planes and a red equal-angular-momentum plane."}

The rank labels count the independent rotation planes occupied by the dressing. A rank-two dual dressed phase carries one electric-charge component outside the core; rank four carries two; rank six carries three. Equal-charge surfaces determine where these possibilities meet. Similarly, grey galaxies distinguish dressing in one or both angular-momentum planes. These are different outcomes of the same constrained entropy problem, rather than separate assumptions about unrelated solutions.

The known core black holes satisfy a nonlinear density relation, with lowercase charges normalized by $N^2$:

$$
\displaystyle\frac{j_{1}j_{2}}{2}+q_{1}q_{2}q_{3}=\left(q_{1}+q_{2}+q_{3}+\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(q_{1}q_{2}+q_{1}q_{3}+q_{2}q_{3}-\frac{1}{2}(j_{1}+j_{2})\right),
$$

The second ingredient, the unobstructed saddle conjecture, addresses the index. It assumes that the alternating signs do not suppress the leading exponential contribution selected by the largest supersymmetric entropy along an index line. Combining this assumption with the first maximization predicts nine index phases. One is dominated by the ordinary intersection black hole; the other eight are dominated by grey-galaxy or dual-dressed configurations. Thus agreement between the index and the intersection black hole is expected only in part of charge space.
:::

## Microscopic evidence and index phases

![Figure 2. Numerical indicial entropy $N^{-2}\log|n_I|$ at $N=10$, with $2(Z_1+Z_2+Z_3)+3(Z_4+Z_5)=90$, as a function of $j_R=(Z_4-Z_5)/N^2$. Red dots are numerical data. Blue curves give the intersection-black-hole entropy and orange gives the grey-galaxy entropy; the combined solid curve is the prediction under the unobstructed saddle conjecture. ([arXiv:2501.17217](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17217))](../assets/papers/2501.17217/N10GG.svg){fig-alt="Red numerical index data compared with blue black-hole and orange grey-galaxy predictions."}

The field-theory index supplies an independent comparison at $N\leq10$. On the charge slice shown above, the numerical data follow the pure-black-hole curve near the central region and then track the grey-galaxy prediction as the angular-momentum imbalance grows. The transition changes which core supplies the leading entropy. It is visible even at these moderate ranks because the selected slice separates the two predictions and keeps the graviton contribution relatively small in the discriminating region.

The two conjectures organize different aspects of this microscopic picture. Supersymmetric descendants give concrete examples of black holes carrying additional angular momentum. Probe dual giants and directly enumerated field-theory states support the possibility of electric-charge dressing. These examples motivate the dressed concentration prescription, which maximizes over the known single-center black-hole family. The more tentative unobstructed saddle assumption then relates that positive degeneracy problem to the signed sum defining the index. Qualitative agreement with finite-$N$ data provides evidence for the combined prediction on the studied charge slices.

In the grand canonical description, the phase structure has a simple chemical-potential interpretation. In a grey-galaxy phase, the angular-momentum component stored in the dressing is associated with a vanishing renormalized angular potential. In a dual-dressed phase, the corresponding electric potential vanishes. A growing amount of charge can then reside outside the core while the relevant potential remains pinned to its phase boundary. The rank of the dressing records how many independent charge components participate in this redistribution.

This picture explains both the familiar entropy match and its predicted extensions. When the optimal point on an index line is the intersection black hole, the leading index agrees with its area-law entropy. When the optimum moves into a dressed phase, the entropy is instead set by a different core whose remaining charges are supplied by the exterior excitations. The nine-phase index diagram is therefore the projection of a richer eleven-phase ground-state problem, with the index retaining four independent combinations of the five conserved charges.
:::
